curriculum.lesson_evidence: The Nile’s annual flood (in the period studied) deposited fertile silt and shaped irrigation, calendars and settlement. Geographers and historians link environment to human activity using maps and records—without claiming the river 'caused' every belief.
curriculum.scope_limit: Proposed Stage 4 NESA HSIE alignment using catalogue outcome code GE4-1; content-point mapping remains pending. Local First Nations protocols and Community verification remain pending human review. Do not invent Country names, Dreaming stories, sacred knowledge or unverified cultural claims.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
Explain two ways the Nile supported farming and one geographic constraint of desert margins.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: Flood/silt/irrigation named; desert as limit on settlement; based on class sources.

WATCH FOR
Treating the Nile as magic rather than a physical system people managed.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Produce an environment–society diagram for the Nile with six labelled links and a short paragraph on uncertainty in ancient environmental data.

Write a short reflection naming one source or idea you corrected and why.
